summary: The same egg-colouring activity occurs with I kṣuʕənne and III maṣuʕina; object semantics cannot decide the stem. The prefix and registered bases distinguish them.

Detransitive Preterit ṣwiʕi presents the coloured patient state in 112/334. The inherited Detransitive Infinitiv ṣwoʕo also functions as an ordinary active event noun; its box position is preserved without inferring a Detransitive event.
Body-part possessive objects (hands) and ruḥe reflexives retain active morphology. There is no evidence here for a distinct cosmetic, animal or reciprocal-wounding sense.
111/38 has semoqo 'red', whereas the edition translation says weiß. Verify which colour the source intended; keep both supplied readings unchanged in the new quotation.
Reconcile the inherited NE_254;11 reference with supplied MAC NE interview 1/14 before changing citation metadata.
Correct farben to färben
rationale: The verb meaning to dye is färben. The unaccented farben is an inherited typo, also present in the supplied corpus translation; the Turoyo ṣoʕət and the stem gloss färben establish the intended word.

summary: Eggs, yarn, hands, a fox and game knucklebones undergo colouring. Active ruḥo and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe change participant relations without creating a Detransitive form or a new lexical sense.
Reciprocal staining with blood in 60/25 parallels the existing I example; wounding is a contextual consequence, not a separate meaning of the colouring verb.
